description: The four canonical scenarios that anchor the investor demo films. Each one references the canonical athlete archetype + Vault entry that grounds George's response. The UI uses this manifest to render a 'play this scenario' picker on the Scenarios page and to seed pre-recorded conversations for filming.

scenarios.title: AFLW Caffeine — Empathetic Dialogue
scenarios.summary: George leads with empathy, asks one clarifier, then walks Mia from 5 No Doz to 3 mg/kg gum at quarter-time. Models the 3 Rs visibly, lands the privacy reassurance early, closes on N-of-1.
demonstrates: Empathy-first opening under pre-match anxiety
One question per turn — never stacked
Female-athlete sport-specific reframe (3 mg/kg, not the male 6–7 mg/kg)
Quarter-time / half-time strategy as the AFLW-specific lever
Skip-if-not-needed flexibility
Batch-tested certification + sports-science team loop-in
N-of-1 closing

athlete.name: Mia
athlete.level: Professional, with a demanding day job
athlete.context: Semi-final, night game, big crowd, high anxiety, work day after, building toward Grand Final. Slow caffeine metaboliser (can't tolerate coffee after 4pm). Recording note: scenarios 1 and 2 are captured together as one continuous Mia↔George flow — dialogue first, then the full-text answer in the same conversation.

scenarios.opening_question: Louise, I really need your help. We're in the semi-final — a night game — and I'm already more nervous than usual because of the big crowd. I've been taking five No Doz tablets about an hour before important day games, same as the male players do. Should I just do the same thing tonight? The thing is, I can't even have a coffee after 4pm without lying awake half the night. I've got work the next morning in a demanding job, and if I'm wrecked for three or four days I won't be able to train properly before the Grand Final. I want to give everything tonight, but I don't want to blow up my whole week.
scenarios.video_treatment: Voice-first. George's voice plays as text streams onto screen. Six-turn exchange. Confidence pill shifts from moderate (after Q1) to high (after the in-game-strategy turn). Final frame: the Vault citation + 'batch-tested certified' badge.

scenarios.title: AFLW Caffeine — Full Text Answer
scenarios.tagline: Same Mia, same question, full written reply.
scenarios.summary: Same athlete, same question — but Mia just wants the whole thing in one go. George delivers the nine-section structured answer, still in his voice, with the Wise Crowd cited where the in-game options come from.
demonstrates: Posed-question mode — structured nine-section scaffold
Same expertise as the dialogue scenario, expressed once
Wise Crowd cited inline ('Our Wise Crowd suggested…')
ADRV / contamination flag as a first-class point
Post-competition sleep treated as a real strategy, not an afterthought

athlete.name: Mia
athlete.level: Professional, with a demanding day job
athlete.context: Same as scenario 1 — but Mia wants the full text answer this time, not a back-and-forth. Scenarios 1 and 2 are recorded together as one continuous Mia↔George flow in a single session.

scenarios.opening_question: Give me the full thing in one go. I'm a 28-year-old female AFLW player, professional but I still have a day job. We're in the finals and they're playing them at night to get the big crowds. Should I take pre-match caffeine like I do before important day games and just like the male players in the club — five No Doz tablets an hour before? I can't sleep after night matches (in fact I can't even drink coffee after 4pm and still get a good night's sleep), and I have to work the next day in a demanding job. I'm worried it will take me 3–4 days to get back to normal and I won't get to train effectively before then. We need to play as hard as possible to win. How do I get the best from caffeine and bounce back?
scenarios.video_treatment: Text-first. Camera slowly scrolls the structured answer as voiceover reads it. Highlight the nine numbered sections as they appear. Final frame: Wise Crowd badge.

scenarios.title: 100 km Mountain Ultra — Caffeine + Self-Testing Loop
scenarios.tagline: Coco, 38, ~50 kg, sub-12-hr 100 km ultra. Multi-turn.
scenarios.summary: George moves from general advice (6–8 mg/kg distributed across a long, hot day) to a six-session long-run self-test plan, pulls in Garmin/Strava/TrainingPeaks, and frames the athlete as a case study of herself.
demonstrates: Multi-turn chat with deepening detail
Total dose before timing (architecture)
Three caffeine models / protocols A/B/C compared
Heat caveat — caffeine supports execution, doesn't override cooling
Withdrawal warning
Six-session long-run test with logged variables
Connected-platform integration (Garmin, Strava, TrainingPeaks)
N-of-1 ('case study of yourself') framing

athlete.name: Coco
athlete.sport: Trail / ultra running — 100 km mountain ultra
athlete.context: First 100 km mountain ultra in 8 weeks. Hot, exposed midsummer race. Goal sub-12 h. Nervous about caffeine + heat + gut on a new distance. Plans 6 long runs of 9–10 hours. ChatGPT and Claude run side-by-side during this recording to show the generic-AI difference.

scenarios.opening_question: I'm Coco, 38, around 50 kg. I've done a few road marathons but I'm pivoting into ultras — I've got my first 100 km mountain ultra in 8 weeks. Midsummer race, so it'll be hot and exposed up high. I am hoping to finish in under 12 hours.
scenarios.video_treatment: Text-first, ~8 turns. Final beat: the protocol table renders inline, then a 'connected to Garmin' tile lights up to show the data path. Voice intro could be a 5-second 'Hey Coco, let's dig into your first 100.'

scenarios.title: Race Walk — Postponed at the Start Line
scenarios.tagline: World Champs 20 km. Storm. Two-hour delay.
scenarios.summary: Max at the start line, already loaded with bicarb + caffeine, race postponed two hours by electrical storm. George opens with the reframe (threat → opportunity), walks fuelling/hydration, holds caffeine, then channels an anonymised Wise-Crowd panel member in-line for the bicarb piece — blood-bicarb depletes by tactics, not time. Sticks with the plan. Section lead-ins land bold and colour-highlighted.
demonstrates: Empathy under acute, high-stakes pressure
Reframe (threat → opportunity) as the opening move
Holding the plan is the recommendation — not 'do more'
Bold, colour-highlighted section lead-ins (fuelling, caffeine, bicarb, closing)
In-line Wise Crowd: an anonymised panel member channelled for the bicarb domain
Honest uncertainty about an emerging area (bicarb in endurance)
Confidence-restoration close, no false certainty

athlete.name: Max
athlete.context: On the starting line. Pre-race meal + 20 g bicarb + 200 mg caffeine gum already in. Electrical storm has just postponed the race by 2 hours. Has never encountered this before; nervous. Recording note: Max records this scenario; the Wise Crowd responds right after George's answer.

scenarios.opening_question: Hey George, it's Max. This is crazy. I am on the starting line of the 20 km race walk at the World Championships. I had my usual pre-race meal (carbohydrate based, with a cup of coffee) two hours before the event, along with my sodium bicarbonate loading protocol. This is where I have 20 g of bicarb in capsules (~300 mg/kg) with 1600 ml of fluid to give me the benefits of a fluid load as well as extra buffering capacity for my race. Then I had a 200 mg dose of caffeine from gum while I was in the call room, waiting to move to the race start. However, an electrical storm has come through and the race has been postponed for 2 hours. What should I do? I'm feeling pretty nervous anyway because this is something I have never encountered before. Do I top up my caffeine and bicarb doses before I start? I usually take another 200 mg caffeine at the 15 km mark of the race but now I don't know if I will have too little or too much on board to execute my race depending on whether I take more now. How much should I use if I decide to top up?
scenarios.video_treatment: Text-first with calm voice overlay. The opening reframe lands first, then George 'taps the network' — an animated pill labelled 'Wise Crowd panel member' fades in as the bicarb section delivers. Confidence pill is moderate-high — honest about the emerging area. Close on 'You've got this!'

production_notes.voice_intro_template: A 10–20 second voice-first opener at the start of each demo where George introduces himself and the athlete by name. Recorded in the calibrated older-counsel register. Audio overlaid on the WhatSupp UI showing the first chat bubble streaming in.
production_notes.audio_chat_blend: Scenarios 1 and 4 use voice + text combined — voice carries the opener and the emotional turns; text carries the protocol detail. Scenarios 2 and 3 are text-primary; voiceover reads on top for the demo film.
